My experience of it is rather different:

When you are at the point that you don't know what to choose and hence resort to randomness, the outcome will not just be accepted. You suddenly ponder if not some/the other option would be better because XYZ. You are not willing to just go for the randomly chosen option, because making a choice in the given situation is too important (e.g. with what movie you're about to spend your evening after work). The experience of just making any decision has faced you with the gravity of making a decision, and this instills further pondering of the options. Basically, your will to find the best answer has been rekindled, and you're now thinking on a slightly higher resolution and with more experience than before. You found out that you're not quite beyond making a rational decision yourself yet, so your will to use randomness is revealed to have just been laziness (or unawareness that you still had resources).

Rinse and repeat until either the random outcome is accepted or the additional reasoning has lead to a choice.
